package: @astryxdesign/core

# BottomSheet

A mobile touch surface for filters, actions, forms, and detail views that should rise from the bottom of the viewport. For a multi-step flow, give each step its own sheet and one state value that names the open step (see Replacing a sheet); open a second sheet over the first when a step should stay visible beneath it.

Stacking. Every sheet keeps its own isOpen. Open a sheet while another scrim sheet is open and it stacks on top: the sheet beneath stays mounted with its scroll position and inputs, recedes behind the new one (the nearest covered sheet shrinks to 0.96 and lifts 8px, deeper ones to 0.92 and 16px), and is blocked from pointer, keyboard, and assistive technology by the top sheet's modal dialog. The sheets can be siblings, live in separate components, sit inside another sheet's content, or sit inside a BottomSheetSwitcher step; a whole switcher is one level, and switching its step in place does not change its position. Nothing moves in the DOM: each sheet's dialog stays where it is written, and no wrapper component is needed.

Order is open order. The top sheet is the one presented most recently that is still open; a sheet that closes and reopens comes back on top. When several sheets open in one update (a deep link into a flow), there is no open order between them, so tree order decides: a sheet below the sheets rendered in its content, siblings in the order they are written. That order is right in the first painted frame.

One scrim. Only the bottom sheet's backdrop dims the page; the backdrops of the sheets above it are transparent, so a stack never darkens per level. The dim holds steady while sheets push and pop, and if the bottom sheet closes while sheets remain above it, the next sheet's backdrop takes over in the same frame.

Dismissal. Escape, a tap on the scrim, a downward swipe, and a platform close request (Android back, a close watcher) reach only the top sheet, through that sheet's own onOpenChange, and that sheet's purpose applies: required blocks all of them, form blocks the scrim and the swipe. Nothing closes a whole stack at once; set every sheet closed in one update when a flow is done and they leave together.

Closing a covered sheet from code. Sheets rendered inside the closing sheet's content are part of it: they are presented only while it is open and leave with it. Their isOpen stays yours, as with a Dialog rendered in a closed Dialog: nothing is written to it, and a nested sheet that is still open when its host reopens is presented again, on top. Set it closed yourself when the flow is done. Sheets above the closing sheet that are not in its content stay open and keep their order; the closing sheet slides out from beneath them, and if it owned the scrim, the sheet above takes it over.

Replacing a sheet. Close the top sheet and open another in the same update (one state value that names the open step does this) and the new sheet replaces it instead of stacking on it: the new sheet rises above the one it replaces; if the replaced sheet is taller it moves down to meet the new sheet's top edge at the same time; the replaced sheet fades only after both motions finish, and is inert and hidden from assistive technology from the start. The scrim holds steady throughout, with no dip; focus moves into the new sheet; and when the flow closes, focus returns to the element that opened its first sheet, whichever sheet closed last. This is the handoff the deprecated BottomSheetSwitcher ran between its steps; a multi-step flow needs no switcher: give each step its own BottomSheet and one state value. A replace happens only when exactly one sheet closes and one opens in the update, the closing sheet was the top sheet of its stack, and the move was made from inside it (the control last pressed, or with no recent press the focused element, was in the closing sheet, as a step's own Continue or Back button is); a covered sheet closing while a sheet opens, a close and an open in different updates, or a close and an open driven from a control outside the closing sheet (two unrelated owners acting at once) keep the ordinary push and pop motion and their own focus return. A replace over an open stack runs one level up and leaves the sheets beneath covered. Non-modal sheets (hasScrim={false}) replace each other the same way, with no scrim: they are hosted in the browser top layer as manual popovers, so the entering step orders above the retained one with no page-level z-index, and toasts raised before or while the sheet is open stay above it. Below the Popover API support floor (Tier 2 in the browser support guide) the sheet falls back to show() in page stacking order: usable, but with no promise over later page content. A non-modal sheet returns focus to its opener on close only while focus is still inside it; focus taken elsewhere on the live page stays there.

Focus. Opening a sheet, modal or not, focuses its data-autofocus field (a TextInput with hasAutoFocus) in every browser. Without one, focus goes wherever the engine's native dialog focusing steps land: the panel in Chromium, the first focusable control in Firefox. A step entering as a replacement also focuses a data-autofocus descendant first, so a flow that opens on a field keeps the keyboard on it. Closing the top sheet returns focus into the sheet it reveals: to the control that opened it when that control is still there, otherwise to the revealed sheet's panel. When the last sheet closes, the standalone rules apply: finalFocusRef, else the element that opened the sheet, with a focus ring only after keyboard input. When every sheet of a stack closes in one update, focus returns once, to the bottom sheet's finalFocusRef or opener, after the last dialog has closed.

Caveats. A Dialog, AlertDialog, or Popover opened from a sheet paints above the sheet and does not make it recede; a sheet opened from inside that Dialog paints above the Dialog and stacks over the sheet beneath. Sheets with hasScrim={false} stay out of the stack entirely (they replace each other, but never stack, recede, or take the scrim). A sheet React hides (a suspended Suspense boundary, Activity mode="hidden") leaves the stack and closes its dialog; when it is shown again it is presented again, on top. Only sheets rendered in the same document stack; a sheet inside an iframe is its own stack.

**Import:** `import {BottomSheet} from '@astryxdesign/core/BottomSheet';`

## Anatomy

| Element | Required | Description |
|---------|----------|-------------|
| Sheet panel | Yes | Painted surface that rises from the bottom edge and contains the sheet. |
| Content area | Yes | Padded, scrollable container that presents the caller-provided sheet content. |
| Handle | Yes | Decorative grab affordance and drag region at the top of the panel. |
| Scrim | No | Backdrop that dims and blocks the page in a scrim-backed presentation. |

## Best Practices

- **Do:** Use for mobile-first surfaces (filters, share sheets, quick actions) where the content should rise from the bottom edge.
- **Do:** For a drill-in, open the next sheet over the current one and keep each sheet's isOpen where its data lives; a detail sheet can sit inside the list sheet that opens it, right next to the row. Close every sheet in one update to close the whole flow.
- **Do:** Pick the starting height that fits the content: 'hug' for short bounded content, 'capped' for lists, and 'tall' for forms or streaming/resizing content.
- **Do:** Use purpose='form' to protect entered data from scrim clicks and swipes while keeping Escape available; reserve purpose='required' for flows that must end through an explicit action.
- **Don't:** Don't make the sheet content overly long. Break it into steps, each its own sheet, with one state value naming the open step; moving on replaces one with the next.
- **Don't:** Don't stack more than two or three sheets: deeper sheets share the second recede step and the user has to pop them one at a time. Replace steps instead (close one, open the next in one update) when they do not need to stay visible.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `isOpen` | `boolean` | - | Whether a standalone sheet is open. Fully controlled; pair with onOpenChange. Omitted only inside the deprecated BottomSheetSwitcher, which drives its steps itself. |
| `onOpenChange` | `(isOpen: boolean) => void` | - | For a standalone sheet, called when it requests an open-state change. Automatic calls follow purpose: info dismisses on Escape, scrim click, or swipe; form dismisses on Escape only; required never dismisses implicitly. Omitted only inside the deprecated BottomSheetSwitcher, which drives its steps itself. |
| `finalFocusRef` | `RefObject<HTMLElement \| null>` | - | Optional explicit focus-return target for a standalone sheet. Use when the opener can remount or the active element is not a reliable trigger, such as an adaptive presentation switch. Always focused when the sheet closes on its own or last; when a modal sheet is still open beneath, focus returns into that sheet (to this element if it is inside it, else the revealed panel). Omitted only inside the deprecated BottomSheetSwitcher, which drives its steps itself. |
| `purpose` | `'required' \| 'form' \| 'info'` | `'info'` | Controls implicit dismissal behavior, matching Dialog. info allows Escape, scrim click, and swipe-to-dismiss. form protects entered data by blocking scrim click and swipe while allowing Escape. required blocks every implicit dismissal path and uses role='alertdialog'. Explicit controls may still update the controlled state. Works for standalone and BottomSheetSwitcher-managed sheets. |
| `sheetId` | `string` | - | Deprecated with BottomSheetSwitcher: give each step its own standalone sheet with isOpen instead. Still works as released: the unique ID of this sheet inside a BottomSheetSwitcher, which opens it when activeSheet matches; omit isOpen and onOpenChange when sheetId is used. |
| `label` | `string` | - | Accessible label for the sheet. Required; the sheet has no built-in heading to derive a name from. **(required)** |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | - | Sheet content in a scrollable area. The named body is keyboard reachable while overflowing. Forward Tab entry may move directly to the first native link or button; input controls, composite widgets, and nested scroll areas retain the body stop. Shift+Tab from a delegated first child skips the body. Fitting content adds no body stop. The internal observed content box preserves block flow and percentage heights. If it includes a text-entry control that can bring up the mobile keyboard, use height='tall' and keep the sheet fully expanded while editing. **(required)** |
| `padding` | `0 \| 0.5 \| 1 \| 1.5 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5 \| 6 \| 8 \| 10` | - | Internal padding of the sheet content using the spacing scale, matching Dialog. When omitted, uses the theme default for bottom sheets (--spacing-4 unless the theme sets padding on bottom-sheet). A lone Section child escapes the padding, and bleed children such as Table and Divider compensate against it. Use 0 for edge-to-edge content that supplies its own inset. Whatever the padding, the block-start inset is never less than the grab bar's height (--spacing-6), so resting content starts below the bar. |
| `height` | `'hug' \| 'capped' \| 'tall' \| number \| string` | `'capped'` | How tall the sheet is. Named budgets: 'hug' fits its content up to 92% of the viewport, 'capped' is a scrolling mid-height panel (~62%), and 'tall' is a pinned near-full panel (~92%) for content that streams in. Or pass a number (px) / CSS length for a custom budget. Give snapPoints to let the user drag between heights. On shorter viewports the sheet fills the available height. Only a fully expanded 'tall' sheet provides mobile-keyboard accommodation: it stays put and scrolls each focused control above the keyboard. Hug, Capped, numeric and CSS-length heights never do, and a Tall sheet stops doing it the moment the user drags it to a shorter detent, resuming when they drag it back. Outside that state the sheet neither moves nor adds keyboard scroll space, and the browser's own focus reveal is left in place; on iOS that reveal can shift the whole page. This accommodation applies where the visual viewport shrinks for the keyboard, as in Safari on iOS, Firefox for Android and Chrome on Android, where the sheet places the focused control just above the keyboard as it comes up, and the control rides the rest of Gboard’s slide up, and the slide down after it loses focus; a hide Chrome reports late, such as Back, rides down from Chrome’s report (`astryx docs browser-support`). |
| `snapPoints` | `ReadonlyArray<number \| string>` | - | Extra heights the sheet can rest at when dragged; its own height is always the tallest stop, and omitting this gives a sheet that only opens and closes. Each stop is the sheet's visible height: a number is a viewport fraction (0.5 is half the screen), '50%' the same in CSS, '320px' an absolute length. A stop of a quarter of the sheet or less is a peek: it slides away instead of reflowing, and thins the scrim. |
| `hasScrim` | `boolean` | `true` | For a standalone BottomSheet, whether to render a scrim, the semi-transparent overlay that covers and blocks the background. true (default) uses showModal(): top layer, native focus containment, ::backdrop scrim, body scroll lock, and tap-scrim-to-dismiss when purpose='info', with the background inert. A scrim sheet also takes part in stacking (see Stacking below). false presents the sheet in the top layer as a manual popover (below the Popover API support floor, show() in page stacking order as a reduced fallback) with no scrim, no focus trap and no scroll lock, leaving the page behind interactive and scrollable; a no-scrim sheet neither stacks nor is stacked on, but no-scrim steps replace each other with the same handoff. A no-scrim sheet shown while a modal (a scrim sheet or a Dialog) that does not contain it is open is inert under that modal and stays beneath it (show(), no page-level z-index) until that modal has gone, then enters the top layer; a modal mid-exit counts as gone, and rendered inside the modal the sheet enters the top layer at once. In a multi-step flow, set hasScrim the same on every step. |

## Examples

### Basic

```tsx
const [isOpen, setIsOpen] = useState(false);
<BottomSheet
  isOpen={isOpen}
  onOpenChange={setIsOpen}
  label="Filters">
  <FilterControls />
</BottomSheet>
```

### Tall sheet (a list)

```tsx
const [isOpen, setIsOpen] = useState(false);
<BottomSheet
  isOpen={isOpen}
  onOpenChange={setIsOpen}
  label="Nearby places"
  height="tall">
  <PlaceList />
</BottomSheet>
```

### Collapsible to half the screen

```tsx
const [isOpen, setIsOpen] = useState(false);
<BottomSheet
  isOpen={isOpen}
  onOpenChange={setIsOpen}
  label="Nearby places"
  height="tall"
  snapPoints={[0.5]}>
  <PlaceList />
</BottomSheet>
```

### A peek, a working height, and full

```tsx
const [isOpen, setIsOpen] = useState(false);
<BottomSheet
  isOpen={isOpen}
  onOpenChange={setIsOpen}
  label="Route"
  height="tall"
  snapPoints={['96px', '50%']}>
  <RouteDetails />
</BottomSheet>
```

### Hug height (fits content)

```tsx
const [isOpen, setIsOpen] = useState(false);
<BottomSheet
  isOpen={isOpen}
  onOpenChange={setIsOpen}
  label="Share"
  height="hug">
  <ShareActions />
</BottomSheet>
```

### Long scrolling content

```tsx
const [isOpen, setIsOpen] = useState(false);
<BottomSheet
  isOpen={isOpen}
  onOpenChange={setIsOpen}
  label="Release notes"
  height="hug">
  <ReleaseNotes />
</BottomSheet>
```

### Multi-step flow (one sheet at a time, each step replaces the last)

```tsx
// One value names the open step. Moving on closes one sheet and opens the
// next in the same update: the next step rises above the current one, which
// fades once it has arrived. A dismissed step closes the flow.
const [step, setStep] = useState(null);
const stepProps = own => ({
  isOpen: step === own,
  onOpenChange: isOpen => !isOpen && setStep(current => (current === own ? null : current)),
});
<>
  <Button label="Start" onClick={() => setStep('details')} />
  <BottomSheet {...stepProps('details')} label="Details">
    <Button label="Continue" onClick={() => setStep('confirm')} />
  </BottomSheet>
  <BottomSheet {...stepProps('confirm')} label="Confirm">
    <Button label="Back" onClick={() => setStep('details')} />
    <Button label="Done" onClick={() => setStep(null)} />
  </BottomSheet>
</>
```

### Stacked sheets (drill-in: list, order, edit)

```tsx
const [isListOpen, setIsListOpen] = useState(false);
const [orderId, setOrderId] = useState(null);
const [isEditing, setIsEditing] = useState(false);
const closeAll = () => {
  setIsListOpen(false);
  setOrderId(null);
  setIsEditing(false);
};
<>
  <Button label="Orders" onClick={() => setIsListOpen(true)} />
  <BottomSheet isOpen={isListOpen} onOpenChange={setIsListOpen} label="Orders">
    {orders.map(order => (
      <Button key={order.id} label={order.title} onClick={() => setOrderId(order.id)} />
    ))}
  </BottomSheet>
  {/* Opens over the list; the list recedes and stays mounted. */}
  <BottomSheet
    isOpen={orderId != null}
    onOpenChange={open => !open && setOrderId(null)}
    label="Order">
    <Button label="Edit" onClick={() => setIsEditing(true)} />
    <Button label="Close all" onClick={closeAll} />
  </BottomSheet>
  <BottomSheet isOpen={isEditing} onOpenChange={setIsEditing} label="Edit order">
    <Button label="Save" onClick={() => setIsEditing(false)} />
  </BottomSheet>
</>
```

### Detail sheet inside the list sheet that opens it

```tsx
function PlaceRow({place}) {
  const [isOpen, setIsOpen] = useState(false);
  return (
    <>
      <Button label={place.name} onClick={() => setIsOpen(true)} />
      {/* Rendered in the list sheet's content: stacks above it, leaves with it, and comes back with it while still open. */}
      <BottomSheet isOpen={isOpen} onOpenChange={setIsOpen} label={place.name}>
        <PlaceDetail place={place} />
      </BottomSheet>
    </>
  );
}

<BottomSheet isOpen={isListOpen} onOpenChange={setIsListOpen} label="Places">
  {places.map(place => <PlaceRow key={place.id} place={place} />)}
</BottomSheet>
```

### Deep link into a stack (several sheets open in one update)

```tsx
// From a URL: list, order and editor open together. With no open order
// between them, tree order decides: the list is at the bottom, the editor on top.
const [isListOpen, setIsListOpen] = useState(() => route.list);
const [orderId, setOrderId] = useState(() => route.orderId);
const [isEditing, setIsEditing] = useState(() => route.edit);
<>
  <BottomSheet isOpen={isListOpen} onOpenChange={setIsListOpen} label="Orders">…</BottomSheet>
  <BottomSheet isOpen={orderId != null} onOpenChange={open => !open && setOrderId(null)} label="Order">…</BottomSheet>
  <BottomSheet isOpen={isEditing} onOpenChange={setIsEditing} label="Edit order">…</BottomSheet>
</>
```

### Mobile keyboard

```tsx
const [isOpen, setIsOpen] = useState(false);
<BottomSheet
  isOpen={isOpen}
  onOpenChange={setIsOpen}
  label="Add a comment"
  height="tall">
  <LongCommentForm />
</BottomSheet>
```

### No scrim

```tsx
const [isOpen, setIsOpen] = useState(true);
<BottomSheet
  isOpen={isOpen}
  onOpenChange={setIsOpen}
  label="Nearby places"
  hasScrim={false}>
  <PlaceList />
</BottomSheet>
```

### Protect form input

```tsx
const [isOpen, setIsOpen] = useState(false);
<BottomSheet
  isOpen={isOpen}
  onOpenChange={setIsOpen}
  purpose="form"
  label="Edit profile">
  <ProfileForm onSave={() => setIsOpen(false)} />
</BottomSheet>
```

# BottomSheetSwitcher

Deprecated: write each step as its own BottomSheet with isOpen, controlled by one state value that names the open step. Closing the top sheet and opening the next in the same update, from a control inside the open step, runs the same replace handoff (see BottomSheet, Replacing a sheet), with no sheetId and no switcher; a step changed from a control outside the flow (a page control, or code after focus left the step) closes and opens with ordinary push and pop motion. BottomSheetSwitcher keeps working until a future minor release removes it: a flow used on its own behaves as released (with three fixes: a toast raised from a step renders above the flow and can be pressed, under reduced motion its steps follow the reduced-motion rule, and a step with a hasAutoFocus field opens on that field in every browser), and a flow stacked with other sheets is one level of the stack (it recedes and is blocked when covered, shares the one scrim, and stands down from dismissal while covered). Modal and hasScrim={false} flows migrate the same way. Set activeSheet to a nested BottomSheet's sheetId to open or switch steps, and to null to close.

Stacking. A scrim flow is one level in the stack of open sheets (see BottomSheet, Stacking). Open it while a standalone sheet is open and the flow sits on top of that sheet, which recedes and is blocked; open a standalone sheet while the flow is open, from a step's content or from anywhere else, and that sheet sits on top while the whole flow recedes as one. Switching the step in place never changes the flow's position. Escape, the scrim, a swipe, and a platform close request reach only the top level: the flow's onActiveSheetChange(null) when the flow is on top, the standalone sheet's onOpenChange(false) when that sheet is. A standalone sheet rendered inside a step's content is presented only while that step is the active one: it leaves when the flow switches step or closes, its isOpen stays yours, and it is presented again, on top, if the step returns while it is still open. Only the bottom level's backdrop dims the page. A no-scrim flow stays out of the stack.

**Import:** `import {BottomSheetSwitcher} from '@astryxdesign/core/BottomSheet';`

## Anatomy

| Element | Required | Description |
|---------|----------|-------------|
| Sheet dialogs | Yes | One native dialog per child sheet, presented and closed by the switcher; the dialog hosting the active sheet carries the flow's ref, id, modality, and dismissal. |
| Sheet panels | Yes | Direct BottomSheet children; exactly one is interactive while a previous panel may remain visible and inert during a handoff. |
| Scrim | No | Native dialog backdrop shown by the default scrim-backed modal presentation; one sheet dialog paints it at a time, so a handoff never dims the page twice. |

## Best Practices

- **Do:** Prefer one standalone BottomSheet per step with one state value naming the open step; the replace handoff is the same and nothing has to be nested under a switcher.
- **Do:** Migrate an existing flow in place: replace activeSheet / onActiveSheetChange with one step value, give each step isOpen={step === id} and a guarded onOpenChange (clear the step only if it is still the open one) in place of sheetId, remove the wrapper and move its hasScrim onto every step. Map the other switcher props: onCancel becomes a guarded onOpenChange on each step (ignore false while the flow must stay open) — a standalone sheet reports Escape, the platform close, the scrim tap and the swipe all as onOpenChange(false) with no reason, so the guard holds the step against all of them while it applies, and a veto of Escape alone has no equivalent; the only per-path lever is purpose (form keeps Escape and blocks the scrim tap and the swipe; required blocks all three and exposes the step as an alertdialog). A consumer aria-label or aria-labelledby becomes each step label, which names its dialog. ref, id, data-testid, className, style, xstyle and the other dialog props have no dialog-level equivalent: a standalone sheet sends its ref and base props to the panel div and its dialog is implementation, so a test or anchor that needs the dialog queries the panel closest("dialog"), and dialog-level styling is dropped.
- **Don't:** Don't split information across sheets when people need to compare it; use a full-page layout that keeps the relevant content visible together instead.
- **Don't:** Don't use a step flow when multiple panels must stay interactive or visible together; a flow intentionally selects one interactive step.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLDialogElement>` | - | Ref resolved to the native dialog hosting the flow: the active sheet's dialog, which changes to the next sheet's on a handoff; the exiting sheet's through its exit; and, while the flow is closed, the dialog that hosted it last (or the first mounted sheet's). It is never null while a sheet is mounted, from the first commit on. id and data-testid render on this dialog only: a flow that mounts open carries them on the active sheet's dialog in server markup too; a flow that mounts closed carries them from the first commit's synchronous re-render on, and its server markup carries them on no element. Other dialog props apply to every sheet dialog. |
| `onCancel` | `(event: SyntheticEvent<HTMLDialogElement>) => void` | - | Called before the switcher handles a native cancel request (Escape or the platform close). Attached to every sheet dialog; the browser raises cancel on the dialog it is presenting, the active sheet's. Calling preventDefault() keeps the controlled flow open. |
| `activeSheet` | `string \| null` | - | ID of the interactive BottomSheet, or null when the flow should close. Match a nested BottomSheet's unique sheetId; the previous sheet may remain visually present and inert while the new sheet enters, simultaneously align downward behind a shorter step, then fade away. **(required)** |
| `onActiveSheetChange` | `(activeSheet: string \| null) => void` | - | Called with null when the active sheet dismisses according to its purpose. Child BottomSheets may use purpose='form' or purpose='required' to limit implicit dismissal while flow controls can still use the same state setter to switch sheets or close the flow. **(required)** |
| `hasScrim` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether the sheet dialogs are modal. true presents each sheet with showModal() for a native ::backdrop, native focus containment, one body scroll lock held for the whole flow, and click-to-dismiss when the active BottomSheet has purpose='info'; only one backdrop paints at a time. false uses show() with no backdrop and leaves the page interactive; avoid transformed, contained, or clipping ancestors because a non-modal dialog remains in its containing context. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | - | BottomSheets identified by unique sheetId values. **(required)** |

## Examples

### Replacement: the same three-step flow as standalone sheets

```tsx
const [step, setStep] = useState(null);

<>
  <Button label="Start" onClick={() => setStep('details')} />
  <BottomSheet isOpen={step === 'details'} onOpenChange={o => !o && setStep(c => (c === 'details' ? null : c))} label="Details" height="hug">
    <SetupDetails />
    <Button label="Continue" onClick={() => setStep('preferences')} />
  </BottomSheet>
  <BottomSheet isOpen={step === 'preferences'} onOpenChange={o => !o && setStep(c => (c === 'preferences' ? null : c))} label="Preferences" height="hug">
    <Preferences />
    <Button label="Back" onClick={() => setStep('details')} />
    <Button label="Continue" onClick={() => setStep('confirm')} />
  </BottomSheet>
  <BottomSheet isOpen={step === 'confirm'} onOpenChange={o => !o && setStep(c => (c === 'confirm' ? null : c))} label="Confirm" height="hug">
    <Confirmation />
    <Button label="Back" onClick={() => setStep('preferences')} />
    <Button label="Done" onClick={() => setStep(null)} />
  </BottomSheet>
</>
```

# BreadcrumbItem

BreadcrumbItem represents one destination, action, current location, or sibling-menu trigger inside a Breadcrumbs trail.

**Import:** `import {BreadcrumbItem} from '@astryxdesign/core/Breadcrumbs';`

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `children` | `ReactNode` | - | Label content for the breadcrumb item. **(required)** |
| `href` | `string` | - | URL the breadcrumb links to; omit for non-navigable items. |
| `onClick` | `(e: MouseEvent) => void` | - | Click handler for the breadcrumb item. |
| `isCurrent` | `boolean` | - | Marks this item as the current page, applying aria-current="page". When omitted, the last item is auto-detected if no item is explicitly current; pass false to opt out. |
| `startIcon` | `ReactNode` | - | Icon rendered before the item label. |
| `menu` | `DropdownMenuOption[] \| ReactNode` | - | Menu opened when the item is activated, using the same item API as DropdownMenu/MoreMenu/ContextMenu (a DropdownMenuOption[] array or composed DropdownMenuItem children). Renders a link-styled menu trigger with a chevron and aria-haspopup="menu". Takes precedence over href/onClick. |
| `menuSize` | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` | - | Size passed to the menu items. Defaults from the breadcrumb variant ('supporting' → 'sm', otherwise 'md'). |
| `as` | `LinkComponentType` | - | Custom link component to render instead of <a>. Overrides the provider-level default from LinkProvider. Only applies to non-current items. |
